Effect of Substitution on the Structure and Magnetic Properties of Transition Metal based Ternary Metal Chalcogenides of General Formula (Fe/Mn)II2AIVS4

Abstract:

Transition metal-based chalcogenides have attracted considerable attention not only due to its remarkable magnetic properties but also due to its diverse structural properties. Apart from their intrinsic magnetic properties, these compounds also show thermoelectric, nonlinear optics, solar cells, superconductivity, magnetocaloric and other applications. Particularly, compounds with the general formula MII2AIVQ4 (M = transition metal A = Si, Ge, Ti, and Sn Q = S, Se, and Te) are found to exhibit rejuvenated research interest because of their distinct structural and complex magnetic properties. This thesis investigates the structural and magnetic properties of ternary transition metal sulfides with the general formula MII2AIVS4 (M = Fe, Mn A = Sn, Si and Ti). The work systematically explores four distinct structure types&mdashcubic spinel, ordered defect rock-salt, olivine, and Cr3S4-type, through controlled cation substitution at both the M and A sites. In the Fe2&minusxCuxSnS4 and Fe2&minusxZnxSnS4 systems, aliovalent Cu+ and isovalent Zn2+ substitution stabilize the cubic spinel structure, induce mixed valence states (Fe2+/Fe3+), and tune the ferrimagnetic ordering temperature. The Mn2&minusxCuxSnS4 series demonstrates a Cu-driven structural phase transition from defect rock-salt to spinel, accompanied by mixed valence (Mn2+/Mn3+) and ferrimagnetic ordering, while the Mn2Sn1&minusxSixS4 series exhibits a Si-driven structural phase transition from defect rock-salt to olivine. The Fe1+xTi2&minusxS4 adopts the Cr3S4-type structure and exhibits a structural and magnetic evolution from a 1D chain-like system to a 3D network as the Fe content increases accompanied by a rise in the magnetic transition temperature from approximately 80 K (x = 0) to 310 K (x = 1). Together, these studies establish a comprehensive structure&ndashproperty relationship in these M2AS4 compounds.
